preconditions.expression: isinstance(stdin, str) and len(stdin) > 0 and all(c in {'A', 'B', 'C', '.'} for c in stdin)
preconditions.description: The input is a non-empty string composed exclusively of 'A' (amber), 'B' (buff), 'C' (canary yellow), and '.' (empty cell).

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'Yes' if any(all(flower in {'A', 'B', 'C'} for flower in {stdin[i], stdin[i-1], stdin[i+1]} if 0 <= i-1 < len(stdin) and 0 <= i+1 < len(stdin)) or (stdin[i] in {'A', 'B', 'C'} and (stdin[i-1] in {'A', 'B', 'C'} or stdin[i+1] in {'A', 'B', 'C'})) for i in range(len(stdin))) else 'No'
postconditions.description: The output is 'Yes' if there exists a cell (index i) in the input string where, after any subset of flowers wither (spreading their color to adjacent cells), the cell contains at least one flower or petal of each color ('A', 'B', 'C'). Otherwise, output 'No'.
